dublinCore.description: Interactive schema validator for MicroSim metadata. A JSON editor shows a document with errors marked in the gutter, and a results panel lists each error or warning with its location path, current value, and expected value. Students click an issue to jump to its line, edit the JSON while it is re-validated live, watch a progress bar count fixed issues, and compare what Auto-fix can and cannot repair.

learningObjectives: Distinguish valid from invalid JSON metadata by analyzing validation feedback
Locate the line that causes a validation error from its message and path
Correct missing required fields, wrong types, invalid enum values, and array constraint violations
Explain the difference between an error and a warning
prerequisites: Knows what required fields, types, and enums are in a JSON Schema

controls.label: Metadata JSON editor
controls.description: Multi-line code editor with line numbers, syntax colors, and issue markers

controls.label: Validate
controls.description: Run the validator and report the number of remaining errors

controls.label: Auto-fix
controls.description: Repair mechanical mistakes such as misspelled keys, wrong quotes, and enum values with an obvious replacement

controls.label: Show hints
controls.description: Show a suggested fix for the selected issue

controls.label: Load Example
controls.description: Three errors, valid, missing required, wrong type, invalid enum, array error, or misspelled key

instructionalStrategies: Classify each error before fixing it
Compare what Auto-fix can repair with what needs human judgment

assessmentQuestions.question: Why can a document be valid JSON but invalid metadata?
Fix the three-error example without using hints.
